title: 📜 History & Ancient Lore
rawNotionMarkup: This page records broad historical canon, ancient civilisations, established historical accounts, disputed traditions and accepted seeds for future discoveries. It is separate from the dated campaign chronicle and from the present-day investigation of the eastern mine. ## Historical evidence and uncertainty Eryndor's history is incomplete. Records may be fragmentary, biased, mistranslated, lost, deliberately altered or preserved in contradictory traditions. A story's existence is evidence that a tradition is told; it does not automatically prove every detail in the story. - Established: Supported as a fact of the setting or by reliable historical evidence. - Reported: Preserved in a source or testimony, but not independently confirmed. - Disputed: Multiple accounts conflict, and no settled answer is established. - Hypothesis: A possible explanation, not a confirmed fact. - Open: Deliberately unresolved. - Future mystery seed: A potential discovery to use later; it has not yet happened in the campaign. The ancient past is not controlled by one civilisation. Not every ruin is First Throne-built, not every magical mystery involves the moons, and not every ancient discovery is connected to Natural Magic or the same lost technique. ## The First Throne The First Throne was a continent-spanning Khazari civilisation, with a population that may have exceeded 40 million at its height. The figure is an estimate, not a census. The civilisation had settlements across the Ironspine region and was one of the greatest achievements in Khazari history. It was sophisticated rather than primitive. Established features attributed to it include: - Advanced rune-powered machinery. - Extensive underground agriculture. - Magical communication networks. - Sophisticated fortifications. - Large-scale engineered subterranean structures and systems. - A level of runic and engineering knowledge beyond what most modern Khazari institutions can reproduce. The First Throne was not merely an early version of the modern Seven Mountain Thrones. Its scale, institutions and technical achievements were exceptional. ### Abandonment and dissolution The First Throne appears to have been deliberately abandoned through an organised process rather than destroyed in a conventional war. The precise reasons remain unknown. Possible explanations include political dismantling, deliberate erasure of institutions, fear of allowing later rulers to claim its legitimacy, or a response to a danger that the civilisation could no longer manage. These are interpretations, not settled history. Do not select one explanation as canon without evidence. The transition from the First Throne to the later Seven Mountain Thrones is not fully documented. The exact founding dates, succession lines, territorial changes and role of surviving institutions remain open. ### Sovereigns and the end - Thargrim the Deepfather: A legendary founder or early sovereign of the First Throne. The exact historical details of his life and reign are not established here. - Thargrim IV: The last universally acknowledged sovereign of the First Throne. His ultimate fate is disputed. Three enduring accounts of Thargrim IV's fate survive: 1. He sacrificed himself to operate a containment system during the evacuation. 2. He was overthrown by nobles after ordering the abandonment. 3. He survived and led a group east into an unknown underground region. None is proven. Different records or traditions may favour different versions. Do not merge them into one confirmed biography. ## The Silence Below Ancient records describe a sequence of disturbing events roughly three millennia before the Seven Mountain Thrones were formally established. The episodes are commonly grouped under the name the Silence Below. ### c. 3,240 years before the Seven Thrones — Deep Resonance Rhythmic hammering was reported from beneath the First Throne's inhabited territories. At least one settlement was evacuated. The surviving accounts describe a sound that appeared to come from below, but do not establish its source. ### c. 3,190 years before the Seven Thrones — Unlit Halls Magical illumination failed in the Unlit Halls. Survivors reported that something moved in the darkness. The accounts are frightening but do not identify what moved, whether it was a creature, a magical effect, a structural event or something else. ### c. 3,160 years before the Seven Thrones — Final Sealing Containment gates were constructed or activated as part of the final response. The records connect this period to the end of the First Throne's organised presence in the affected deep regions, but the exact sequence of evacuation, sealing and political dissolution is not fully known. An ancient warning survives: > Let no descendant mistake the silence of the deep for the absence of what dwells within. ### What the records do and do not establish Hadrik Ironvein's historical interpretation is that the First Throne may have been trying to escape or contain something it did not understand. He does not know what that was. Possible explanations include a living presence, a magical catastrophe or an event involving something between those categories. None is established. The warning does not prove that an entity remains alive, that a specific sealed door contains it, or that all underground resonances are related. The current eastern mine mystery has its own separate evidence record. The historical parallels are relevant context, not proof of a direct connection. ## Khazari and Eldar antiquity Khazari and Eldar are both ancient peoples. There is no universally accepted creation story establishing which came first. Do not present either as the proven first people of Eryndor or as the sole source of civilisation. Both peoples have long historical traditions, but longevity does not make any one people the exclusive custodian of Eryndor's past. Other peoples and continents preserve independent histories, some of which may contradict familiar Khazari or Eldar accounts. ## Ancient discoveries and independent mystery seeds The world's ancient past is broad, fragmented and not controlled by a single civilisation. The following are future discovery seeds for a living world. They are not established finds in Gloin's current campaign. Introduce them gradually and independently, and allow expeditions to fail, sources to be wrong, and discoveries to remain inaccessible. ### Khazari — The Kingdom Beneath the Kingdom A future expedition may uncover a vast underground city with residential districts, foundries, waterways and machinery more sophisticated than current Khazari engineering. Its builders, age, purpose and abandonment remain unknown. It is not automatically First Throne-built. ### Urakai — The Empire That Wasn't Supposed to Exist Monumental roads, irrigation works, fortifications and treaties may challenge accepted Urakai and continental chronologies. Some inscriptions may refer to peoples thought to have arisen much later. Authenticity, dating and interpretation would need careful examination. ### Human powers of Sahrad — The Buried Fleet Drought or shifting desert sands may expose a fleet of ancient ships far inland. Such a discovery could raise questions about an old maritime civilisation and changed coastlines. It would not by itself prove a global flood or a particular migration. ### Southern Sultanates — The Sleeping Sun An ancient observatory may preserve unusually accurate celestial records, a prediction of a future conjunction and an unexplained reference to “the Sleeping Sun.” The phrase's meaning and the reliability of the prediction remain open. ### Gnomes — The Impossible Engine An ancient apparatus may appear to have operated for millennia without an obvious fuel source. Its intended function, energy source, age and relationship to any larger machine are unknown. It may be misunderstood or not actually self-powered. ### Giants of Tharvorn — The Walking Mountains Enormous symmetrical structures within mountain formations may resemble artificial beings. Giant traditions disagree about whether such beings ever existed. The stories are not proof of a literal race or of a connection to the Living Mountains. ### The Library Without a Location An archive may be discovered with records from many peoples and civilisations. Some dates may conflict with accepted chronologies, and some entries may appear to describe events that have not yet occurred. Provenance, authenticity, chronology and interpretation would all be disputed. ### The Inland Ocean Explorers may discover an immense subterranean sea with distant shores, islands, unfamiliar ecosystems and underwater ruins. Its full extent, origin and connection to surface waterways are unknown. ### The Fallen Star A colossal anomalous object may be found embedded deep underground. Its composition does not match known Eryndoran materials. It may be celestial, magical, artificial or something not yet understood; no explanation is established. ### The City That Was Never Built A complete and apparently preserved city may be found beneath a mountain. Its homes, streets and workshops are equipped, but there is no reliable evidence that inhabitants ever occupied it. Its builders and intended purpose remain unknown. ## Living Mountains in the historical record Living Mountains are genuine, exceedingly rare colossal living beings. Their bodies are so immense and integrated with geology that, while dormant, they can be indistinguishable from ordinary mountain ranges or solitary peaks. A Living Mountain may remain dormant for centuries or millennia. During that time, forests, rivers, caves, snow and even settlements may accumulate across its body. Its movements and timescales are almost impossible for smaller peoples to comprehend. Awakening is extraordinarily rare. It is not caused by ordinary noise, mining or a routine lunar alignment. The conditions that can rouse one are not fully understood and may differ between individuals. If one awakens, terrain may shift, valleys may close, rivers may change course and settlements or fortifications built upon its body may be endangered. A Living Mountain is not automatically hostile or benevolent. Its motives, awareness and relationship with smaller peoples vary and may be difficult to understand. Most people will never witness one awaken. Reports may be dismissed as folklore, earthquakes, landslides or exaggerated traveller tales; reliable evidence is exceptionally scarce. Their existence is established in Eryndor's deeper reality, but their number, locations, origins, names and individual natures remain unknown. They are distinct from Giants and Ents. Do not place one near Gloin or connect one to the eastern mine without a properly developed reason. ## Historical development rules - Keep independent civilisations independent unless evidence establishes contact, borrowing, conquest or shared origin. - Historical accounts should be attributed to their sources when evidence is uncertain. - Do not collapse all ancient knowledge into First Throne history. - A shared symbol or similar engineering technique does not prove a shared civilisation. - A prophecy, legend or unusual inscription is not automatically true. - Ancient discoveries may have economic, religious, scholarly, political and military consequences, but none should exist solely to provide Gloin with a convenient quest. - Add new historical events to a dated timeline only when their dates and status are supported. Current campaign events belong in the Campaign Chronicle.
